title: Associated-prime specialization from a primary closed fibre over a valuation domain
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation domain, meaning an integral domain such that every nonzero element of $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ or its inverse belongs to $A$, and let $\mathfrak m_A$ be its maximal ideal. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, meaning $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$, essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. Let $N$ be a finite $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $\mathfrak q\subseteq B$ be a prime ideal with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=(0)$ and $\sqrt{\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_AB}=\mathfrak m_B$, where $\sqrt I=\{b\mid b^n\in I\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$. Put $B_K=B\otimes_AK$, $N_K=N\otimes_AK$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], let $\mathfrak q_K=\mathfrak qB_K$ (a prime), and put $T=(B_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ and $P=(N_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Suppose the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_T$ is in $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$, with associated primes understood as annihilators of nonzero elements [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. Set $R=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ and $L=N/\mathfrak m_AN$, where $\mathfrak m_AN$ is generated by the elements $\varphi(a)n$ with $a\in\mathfrak m_A$. Then the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_AB$ belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}_R(L)$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph: the radical condition, nonzerodivisor power, use of Tag 0GSG (lemma-mod-injective-valuation-ring), and generic-fibre contradiction, isolated as a local algebra statement.

proof.text: Suppose for contradiction that $\mathfrak m_R\notin\operatorname{Ass}_R(L)$. By [lem-trf-valuation-closed-fibre-noetherian], $R$ is Noetherian: its hypotheses are precisely our local essentially finite type map from the valuation domain $A$. If $n_1,\ldots,n_d$ generate $N$ over $B$, their classes generate $L$ over $R$, since reducing $\sum b_i n_i$ reduces each coefficient $b_i$ modulo $\mathfrak m_AB$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite] gives a finite set $\operatorname{Ass}_R(L)=\{\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_r\}$, each distinct from $\mathfrak m_R$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph, local algebra argument

proof.text: Let $\pi:B\to R$ be the quotient map and $J=\pi(\mathfrak q)$. No $\mathfrak p_i$ contains $J$: otherwise $\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak p_i)$ is a proper prime containing $\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_AB$, so it contains its radical $\mathfrak m_B$ (if $b^e$ is in a prime, then $b$ is in it), and equals $\mathfrak m_B$. Taking images would give $\mathfrak p_i=\mathfrak m_R$, contrary to Step 1. If $r>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] applied in $R$ to the ideal $J$ and these finitely many prime ideals gives $\bar g\in J\setminus\bigcup_i\mathfrak p_i$. Choose $g\in\mathfrak q$ with $\pi(g)=\bar g$. If $r=0$, choose $g=0\in\mathfrak q$; its image also avoids the empty union.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph, local algebra argument

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes], applicable because $R$ is Noetherian, $\bar g$ is not a zerodivisor on $L$. Thus multiplication by $\bar g$ on $L$ is injective: $\bar g(l-l')=0$ forces $l=l'$. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-finite-module-injectivity] to the $B$-linear map $u:N\to N$, $n\mapsto gn$. Both its source and target are finite over $B$, the target is $A$-flat by hypothesis, the map $A\to B$ is local and essentially of finite type, and its closed-fibre map is exactly the injective multiplication map just established. The lemma gives injectivity of $g:N\to N$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph, local algebra argument

proof.text: The fraction field $K$ is the localization of the domain $A$ at $A\setminus\{0\}$: nonzero denominators become units, every element is a fraction, and $a/1=0$ implies $a=0$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] gives $A$-flatness of $K$. Apply [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] over $A$ with flat module $K$ to the injective $A$-linear map $g:N\to N$ of Step 3. It gives injectivity on $K\otimes_A N$, hence on $N_K=N\otimes_A K$: the exchange maps $k\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes k$ and $n\otimes k\mapsto k\otimes n$ are inverse by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and carry multiplication by $g$ to multiplication by $g$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph, local algebra argument

proof.text: Multiplication by $g$ remains injective on $P=(N_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$. Indeed, if $g(v/s)=0$, the localization equality criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $t\notin\mathfrak q_K$ with $tgv=0$ in $N_K$. Step 4 then gives $tv=0$, and the same criterion gives $v/s=0$. The image of $g$ lies in $\mathfrak m_T=\mathfrak q_KT$, since $g\in\mathfrak q$. By $\mathfrak m_T\in\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ and [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], there is $z\in P$ with annihilator $\mathfrak m_T$. Necessarily $z\ne0$, since the annihilator of zero is $T$ and a maximal ideal is proper. But $gz=0$, contradicting the injectivity on $P$. This contradiction proves $\mathfrak m_R\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(L)$.
